alerts.title: DTG-associated weight gain and pre-diabetes risk
alerts.message: Guidelines state DTG-based regimens have been associated with weight gain and that antiretroviral drugs are a major cause of diabetes in PLHIV. DTG should not be used in patients who develop diabetes. This patient gained 17kg and her BMI rose from 25.6 to 32.4 over 18 months on TLD. She now has impaired fasting glucose (118 mg/dL), HbA1c 6.1%, acanthosis nigricans, and a family history of Type 2 diabetes. Evidence for drug attribution: the temporal relationship between DTG initiation and rapid weight gain is strong, and DTG is a recognised cause. Evidence against: baseline BMI was already 25.6 and family history confers independent diabetes risk. Metabolically neutral ARVs (ABC, TDF, 3TC) are recommended for patients at risk of DM.

evidence.recommended_action: Assess for diabetes using DM screening tool. Consider substituting DTG with a metabolically neutral ARV. Counsel on weight loss, diet, and exercise. Monitor fasting glucose and HbA1c regularly.

alerts.title: Missing DM screening and pharmacovigilance monitoring
alerts.message: Guidelines require baseline and ongoing fasting blood glucose monitoring for patients on DTG, with DM risk factor assessment using a screening tool. This patient has multiple DM risk factors (obesity, acanthosis nigricans, impaired fasting glucose, family history) yet no clinician assessment or plan was documented today. No orders for repeat fasting glucose, HbA1c, or formal DM screening were recorded. The guideline algorithm requires reassessment every six months or when clinically indicated, and this encounter is clearly clinically indicated by new metabolic abnormalities.

evidence.recommended_action: Perform DM screening tool assessment today. Order repeat fasting glucose and HbA1c in 3 months. Document a management plan addressing weight, blood pressure, and glycaemic monitoring.

alerts.title: Elevated BP and dyslipidaemia require management plan
alerts.message: Guidelines state the goal of treatment is blood pressure below 140/90 mmHg and that uncontrolled hypertension and blood sugar may cause complications including heart attack, stroke, and chronic kidney disease. This patient's BP is 138/88 mmHg, up from a baseline of 118/74, borderline to the target. She also has a significantly atherogenic lipid profile (LDL 148, HDL 38, triglycerides 212). Her compounding risks — obesity, pre-diabetes, dyslipidaemia, and rising BP — substantially increase cardiovascular risk. No assessment or plan was documented for these abnormalities.

evidence.recommended_action: Document a plan for BP monitoring and lifestyle modification. Order repeat lipid panel. Consider dietary counselling and assess cardiovascular risk to guide further intervention.
